A decrease in blood volume will decrease hydrostatic pres-

from the kidney. Renin stimulates conversion of angioten-
sinogen to angiotensin I, and a second activation converts
angiotensin I to angiotensin II. Increasing amounts of 
angiotensin II stimulate release of aldosterone from the
adrenal cortex. Aldosterone directly inﬂ uences the kidney 
to retain Na. When Na levels increase, increased osmotic
pressure will pull ﬂ uid back into the blood; thus, blood 
volume will increase back to its normal range
 7. Explain how aldosterone and arginine vasopressin can aﬀ ect 
urine volume.
Aldosterone directly inﬂ uences the kidney to retain Na. 
Subsequently, osmotic pressure increases and urine volume 
decreases.
Arginine vasopressin causes ﬂ uid to be reabsorbed in the 
tubules of the kidney. Th is decreases urine volume, result-
ing in increased blood volume.
